We'll produce:

- problem: from abstract: multi-hop QA requires coordinating relational and textual evidence across steps; prior work emphasizes only part of loop.

- method: Co-E, training-free system with synchronized bidirectional graph-text working memory; synchronization cycle consolidates textual memory, extracts relational triples into graph memory, injects graph facts back into generation context.

- key_assumptions: maybe that textual and graph memories can be synchronized; that extracted triples are correct; that a shared memory improves reasoning.

We can extract from abstract: "We argue that this coupling requires bidirectional, within-step co-evolution of graph and text." So assumption: bidirectional coupling is beneficial.

- main_contribution: Propose Co-E, a training-free system achieving strong results on six multi-hop QA benchmarks, improving over comparable baselines.

- datasets: WebQSP, CWQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle (six benchmarks).

- benchmarks: same as datasets.

- baselines: Corpus-Based RAG methods (IRCoT, HopRAG, ComposeRAG, RT-RAG, Search-o1, Search-R1, etc.), Graph-Based KGQA methods (PoG, SubgraphRAG, iQUEST, RoG, GNN-RAG, etc.), also retrieval-augmented generation etc.

- metrics: Hits@1 for KGQA, Exact Match (EM) for text-QA, also LLM-judged accuracy.

- results: As per passages: 72.6 EM on 2WikiMultiHopQA, 70.0 EM on Bamboogle, 74.9 Hits@1 on CWQ; also Hits@1 on WebQSP 85.5 (MCTS) and 85.3 (CoT); etc.

- limitations: limited by quality of evidence it retrieves; cannot reliably correct a wrong fact repeatedly supported by retrieved corpus; trades inference cost for stronger reasoning.

- future work: evaluate larger models, extend smaller-backbone study across all benchmarks, compare shared-memory MCTS with branch-local or reward-gated memory commits, adaptive switch between CoT and MCTS, etc.

- code_availability: "Codebase available at https://github.com/hieum98/wemg" (from abstract footnote).

Now relation_to_idea: need problem/method/evaluation overlap scores (0-1) with basis, and conceptual difference.

Our idea: enrich target triple with local context subgraph from same passage, adaptive repair loop, RL transfer.

This paper: Co-E is about synchronized graph-text memory during inference (training-free). Not about training on enriched triples; it's inference-time memory coupling. So problem overlap: both address multi-hop QA needing coordination of graph and text -> high (~0.8). Method overlap: our idea is about training with context-enriched triples and adaptive repair; theirs is about inference-time bidirectional memory; low overlap (~0.2). Evaluation overlap: both use multi-hop QA benchmarks (HotpotQA, etc.) -> high (~0.7). Conceptual difference: we focus on training data enrichment and repair loop; they focus on inference-time memory synchronization without training.
